extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent drafters, patent agents and patent attorneys (those preparing and prosecuting patent applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, step-by-step guidance for preparing, drafting, filing and prosecuting patent applications (claims, description, drawings, abstracts) with attention to legal requirements and drafting technique across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: The claimed invention must be new — not anticipated by the prior art available to the public at the filing date (or priority date) of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search prior art (patent and non-patent literature); avoid public disclosure before filing (professional tip); consider priority dates; examples and discussion of what 'reads on' prior art are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step / nonobviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must involve an inventive step (be nonobvious) over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the claimed subject matter provides a legally sufficient advancement; examineors compare prior art to claims; jurisdictions vary in tests for obviousness — draft claims and description to emphasize technical contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application / utility
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be capable of industrial application or be useful; it must work or be capable of being reduced to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose how to make and use the invention; include examples, working embodiments and data where relevant to show utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject matter claimed must be the type of invention that is patentable under applicable law (e.g., technical inventions; exclusions such as mathematical algorithms or certain methods of medical treatment may apply in some jurisdictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check national/regional rules for excluded subject matter (e.g., laws on biological material, software, medical methods); when borderline, draft claims and description to emphasize technical/functional features; note that countries differ on software, genetic materials, methods of treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirement (sufficiency / enablement / written description)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must disclose the invention sufficiently clearly and completely so that a person skilled in the art can carry it out (including written description requirements where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the description supports the full scope of the claims; include embodiments, working examples, reference to drawings; beware of introducing new matter when amending; keep clear linkage between claims and description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter specifics for biotechnology/genetic sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Genetic sequences may be patentable if isolated/characterized with a functional purpose; a mere sequence without functional indication is generally not patentable in some jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the function, protein produced or utility of the sequence; check national rules—some countries exclude naturally occurring sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter specifics for computer programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Software as such may be excluded in some jurisdictions, but software-implemented inventions (systems/methods delivering a technical effect) can be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft to highlight a technical effect, system or method, and efficiency or new data-processing approach rather than a pure algorithm; avoid claiming pure mathematical algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: Obtaining invention disclosures from inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain a full invention disclosure from inventors containing title, field, background, description, drawings, testing dates and disclosure history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized invention disclosure forms (Annex B example); collect publications, presentations, NDAs, and dates to evaluate novelty; ensure inventorship information is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying patentable inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze invention disclosures to identify which aspects are potentially patentable and worth claiming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate inventive core from non-inventive details; consider commercial value, freedom-to-operate, prior art landscape; involve technical and legal stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the invention (core inventive concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the core inventive concept that provides the novel technical contribution to be protected by claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus drafting (claims and description) on the core inventive idea; identify embodiments and variations to support broad and fallback claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and record correct inventors — persons who contributed to the claimed inventive features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate inventorship is legally important; document contributions and resolve multi-inventor situations; consider jurisdiction-specific representation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical parts of a patent application (Request, Description, Claims, Drawings, Abstract, Application format)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application should contain a request/formality section, a description, claims, drawings (if applicable), an abstract, and conform to required format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow national/regional application format rules; prepare clear request, well-structured description and an informative abstract; include drawings with reference indicators; ensure formalities to avoid procedural rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare the claims first
rubrics_metrics.description: Drafting claims before the description helps set clear protection goals and ensures the description supports claimed scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use claims to define invention boundaries and then craft description and embodiments to support them; avoids unintended gaps between claims and description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad and narrow claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Include both broad (to maximize scope) and narrow (to ensure allowability) claims in a claim set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance breadth with support in the description; include fallback narrower claims to survive examination; consider claim-dependent structures to cascade fallbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent protection and infringement: all-elements rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement analysis requires that an accused product/process includes all elements of a claim (the all-elements rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims with clear elements and consider variants/alternatives to capture likely infringers; avoid ambiguous claim language that could limit enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts of a claim (claim format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims typically have parts (preamble, transition, body) and must be structured to set out elements/limitations precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate claim grammar and transitional terms; ensure the preamble and body support the intended scope; consider two-part (Jepson-style) claim formats where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar of a claim and other detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must use careful grammar and word choice to avoid ambiguity and unintended limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague terms, undefined relative terms, inconsistent terminology; include definitions in the description; use consistent reference numerals and indefinite/definite articles judiciously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-part claims or improvement claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-part claims (preamble/characterizing portion) are used to define known features and distinguish the invention (often used at EPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using two-part claims, clearly state known features and the characterizing elements; ensure support in description and alignment with prior art arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative elements and Markush claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may recite alternative elements (e.g., 'selected from the group consisting of...') — Markush format commonly used in chemical claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Markush/grouping carefully to avoid ambiguity; provide examples and rationale in the description for alternatives; watch jurisdictional acceptability rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional elements and means-plus-function claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional claim language (including means-plus-function) can be used but may invoke specific interpretation rules in certain jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide corresponding structure or embodiments in the description when using functional language; be aware of U.S. §112(f)/means-plus-function constraints and similar national rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent claims stand on their own and set out the essential elements of an invention without relying on other claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft multiple independent claims of different types (product, method, use) to provide layered protection; ensure each independent claim is adequately supported by the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims add specific limitations to independent claims and provide narrower fallback positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order dependent claims logically; ensure each dependent claim refers properly to the claim it depends on; include useful optional features and preferred embodiments as dependents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple dependent claims refer to more than one preceding claim (e.g., 'dependent on any one of claims 1 to 3').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check jurisdictional rules on multiple dependent claims (allowed/fees); use them judiciously to save claim count while preserving combinations of features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims referring to features of another claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may refer to features in other claims to build hierarchical claim sets and combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure cross-reference clarity and support in the description; follow formal drafting rules for referencing other claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim sets based on set theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Design claim sets deliberately to cover the universe of embodiments using set-theoretic relationships (unions, intersections) among claim elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use claim drafting strategies to cover combinations and alternatives systematically; analyze coverage and gaps using set-theory thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schematic example of drafting a set of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical examples illustrating how to draft complementary independent and dependent claims to cover an invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use schematic examples as templates; ensure real applications include specific technical details and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product claims (basic type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims directed to physical products or apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define structural features and essential components; include materials, configurations and optional features in dependents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process / method claims (basic type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims directed to methods or processes for producing an effect or using a product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List steps in clear sequence; consider claim preambles and possible statutory exclusions (e.g., medical methods in some jurisdictions); include apparatus/product claims as complements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble with the purposive expression 'for'
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a purposive preamble (e.g., 'a device for...') to state purpose/activity in the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that some jurisdictions may treat purposive preambles as limiting or non-limiting depending on context — draft to keep intended scope clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-by-process claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that define a product in terms of the process by which it is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when product cannot be adequately defined by structure alone; be aware of jurisdictional limitations on enforceability and novelty assessment (product-by-process may be judged on product, not process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that define invention by specified parameters or ranges (e.g., concentration, temperature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support ranges and parameters with experimental data and description; specify preferred ranges and provide justification to avoid undue breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: General use claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that assert broad intended uses (general purpose claims) for compositions or devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adequate support and examples of uses in the description; watch legal standards for claims to uses (especially second medical use claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical indication (second medical use) claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims directed to the use of a substance for a particular medical indication, including therapeutic uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow jurisdictional claim formats (e.g., Swiss-type or EPC 2000 formats); include clinical/experimental support for the indication; heed exclusions for medical treatment methods where present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for compositions of matter (chemical formulations, mixtures, compounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List components, concentrations, preparation methods where relevant; include preferred embodiments and examples; consider Markush language for alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biotechnology claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims covering biological materials, organisms, sequences, proteins, and related biotechnological inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide functional descriptions, depositional information where required, and clear experimental support; be attentive to ethical and legal limitations in some jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-implemented invention claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for inventions implemented at least partly on a computer or other programmable apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame claims to emphasize technical effects and implementation details; include system, method and computer-readable medium claim types as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent claim design (strategic design of claim scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate an overall claim strategy to balance broad protection, enforceability, and support; include different claim types and fallback positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider competitors' products, prior art, prosecution history, and enforcement strategy; include dependent claims, multiple claim types, and alternatives to maximize enforceable coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, claim word choice and inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and description must be clear and consistent; define terms and avoid relative/ambiguous expressions that create uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define key terms in the description; avoid conflicting terminology between claims and description; watch for undefined relative terms (e.g., 'substantially', 'about').

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explicit definitions of technical terms and alternative meanings used in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include definitions in the description to control claim interpretation and avoid ambiguity; use examples to illustrate terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and describe the features that distinguish the invention from the prior art and that should appear in claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize inventive features in claims and description; prepare arguments for examination distinguishing claims from cited prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of relative terms (e.g., 'upper', 'lower', 'about') should be managed carefully to avoid vagueness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify relative terms in the description with reference frames, examples and quantitative bounds where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncertainty (avoidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft to minimize legal and technical uncertainty in claim scope and description disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer precise language, concrete examples, numerical ranges, and clear functional descriptions to reduce interpretive disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the word 'in' and other prepositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Small words like 'in', 'on', 'for' can materially affect claim scope and should be used deliberately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider jurisdictional interpretations; define intended usage in description; be consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency (avoid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inconsistencies between claims, description and drawings that could undermine support or clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check all parts of the application; update descriptions if claims are amended; maintain consistent numbering and terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Putting this into practice (practical drafting tips)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples and practice-oriented tips on implementing drafting principles in real applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided diagrams and sample claim sets as drafting templates; perform iterative review with technical inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim variations and modifications of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft description and claims to cover foreseeable variations and modifications of the inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List alternative materials, configurations, parameter ranges, and process steps in the description to support broader claim language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding unnecessary limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include unnecessary limitations in claims or description that would unduly narrow protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious when incorporating examples into claim language; keep illustrative embodiments clearly labelled as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative limitations and disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative claim limitations (exclusions) and disclaimers may be used but have legal and support implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure negative limitations have basis in the disclosure or are allowable disclaimers under applicable law; avoid ad hoc disclaimers without support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims and competing products
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft claim scope with an eye to competing products and likely design-arounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform freedom-to-operate and competitor product analysis; include alternatives and broader functional language where support permits to cover likely infringers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must overcome prior art (prosecution readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be drafted anticipating examiner objections and prior art; include fallback positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare claim amendments and arguments; include multiple claim sets with different distinguishing features; document inventive step rationale in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using multiple claim types for the same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek protection through different claim categories (product, process, use, system, computer-readable medium) to maximize enforceability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each claim type is supported by the description; consider strategic use based on jurisdiction (e.g., method vs product).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring that the description supports the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must provide adequate support for the full scope of the claims to avoid added-matter and enablement rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific embodiments, examples, and explicit disclosure for claim alternatives; avoid attempting to later broaden claims beyond original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should satisfy unity requirements (one general inventive concept per application or claim group) as required by some offices and PCT rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple inventions exist, consider divisional or multiple applications; prepare justification for unity where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim point of view (claim drafting perspective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft claims from the perspective of defining what is to be excluded from others (scope) while ensuring support and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt claim drafting viewpoint that balances enforcement objectives with prosecution practicality and description support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing a patent claim during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made during prosecution often narrow claims — know how to do so without introducing new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure amendments are supported by the original disclosure; understand jurisdictional rules for allowable amendments and timing (e.g., broadening limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of subject-matter exclusions (e.g., discoveries, abstract ideas, certain medical methods, natural phenomena) in target jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft to emphasize technical/industrial application and practical steps to avoid exclusion rejections; tailor claims to local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the invention is shown to have industrial applicability where required (closely related to utility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples, protocols, or descriptions showing practical use or manufacture; for biological inventions provide functional data where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Reading on' a patent claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and draft to control whether claims 'read on' (cover) particular products/processes — important for infringement and validity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise element definitions; consider claim construction principles and likely interpretations by courts/examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction in the courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that courts interpret claims according to established doctrines (e.g., prosecution history, specification) which affect enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft specification to shape favorable claim construction; avoid inconsistent statements that could narrow claim interpretation later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key audiences of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent documents are read by multiple audiences — examiners, competitors, licensees, courts, investors — and should be drafted accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor clarity, technical depth and legal framing to these audiences: clear claims for enforcement, sufficient technical disclosure for enablement, and accessible summaries for business stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order in which to draft a patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended sequence: prepare claims first, then description, drawings, abstract and formal parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following the recommended order aids coherence and ensures description supports claimed scope; use checklists and templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting parts of a description: Title of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a succinct, descriptive title that reflects the technical field and invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep title informative but not limiting; align with claims and field of invention statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting parts of a description: Technical field
rubrics_metrics.description: State the technical field to orient the reader and define the context of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be accurate and broad enough to encompass embodiments without unduly limiting the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting parts of a description: Background art
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe relevant prior art and the technical problem the invention addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame background to highlight shortcomings of prior art and motivate claimed features; avoid admissions that could be used to construe claim scope inadvertently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting parts of a description: Summary of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear summary of the invention and its advantages over prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use summary to introduce key features that will appear in claims; do not limit to only preferred embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting parts of a description: Brief description of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: List and briefly describe each drawing figure and its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate figure references with description and claims; use consistent numbering and reference indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting parts of a description: Description of embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed embodiments showing how to make and use the invention, including working examples where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multiple embodiments, preferred options, experimental data, and variations to support broad claim scope and enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting drawings: Types of drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate drawings (schematics, flowcharts, chemical structures, graphs) to illustrate embodiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow office rules for drawing standards; include necessary detail to support claims; label reference indicators clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting drawings: Reference indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use reference numerals/indicators in drawings and description consistently to identify elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define reference numerals in the description; avoid over-reliance on numerals for claim scope — claims should stand alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting drawings: Level of detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide drawings with sufficient detail to support disclosure but avoid unnecessary limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance illustrative detail with generality; include alternative embodiments and generalized drawings when helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting drawings: Drawings provided by the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate inventor-provided drawings while ensuring they meet formal requirements and adequately support claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and, if necessary, redraw or annotate to meet office standards and to improve clarity for prosecution and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting an abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a concise abstract summarizing the technical disclosure of the application (used for searching and indexing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep abstract informative and within office length limits; avoid claims-like language that could be limiting; follow office formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic / priority filings (filing strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to file domestically first or claim priority from an earlier filing; understand priority date consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File before public disclosure; use priority to secure earliest effective date for novelty; plan international filing timelines (PCT, Paris Convention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filings (international filing strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan foreign protection strategy, choosing jurisdictions and filing routes (direct national, PCT) according to commercial and legal priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider costs, enforcement likelihood, market presence, and national patentability rules; use PCT for international phase when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent office procedures and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of procedural steps, timelines, and fees (filing, search, examination, renewal) in target offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for fees and prosecution costs; monitor deadlines and fee schedules; use local counsel when required for formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing procedures in specific jurisdictions (USPTO, EPO, PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow jurisdiction-specific procedures and formal requirements for filing and prosecution (examples: USPTO, EPO, PCT guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult office guides and rules (e.g., EPO Guidelines, PCT Applicant’s Guide); adapt claim formats (two-part claims at EPO), fee structures and timing to each office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond promptly and substantively to office actions, addressing prior art rejections, formal objections and clarity issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare argued responses, amendments supported by the description, and consider interviews; meet deadlines to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting responses to office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft persuasive responses combining legal arguments, claim amendments and technical evidence where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear claim amendments with support; provide prior art distinctions and technical explanations; consider examiner interviews to resolve issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments: Principle and basic requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments must comply with rules (no added matter, supported by original disclosure) and should be principled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check amendment scope against original filing; document basis for each amendment; avoid broadening beyond original disclosure in ways prohibited by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining original disclosure and new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether proposed amendments introduce new matter not present in the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare amendment wording to original description and drawings; if new matter would be introduced, seek alternative supported amendments or file divisional/new application where allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening claims and adding claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand rules and risks when broadening claims or adding new claims after filing (often restricted after certain stages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe jurisdictional limits on broadening amendments; use divisional/continuation strategies when additional claim scope is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting claims allowed: Interviews and prosecution strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use examiner interviews, strategic amendments and arguments to obtain allowance of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare concise claim charts, prior art comparisons, and emphasize inventive distinctions; manage prosecution tactics (conservative vs aggressive amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to second office action and final office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle successive rejections with appropriate strategy — amendments, arguments, requests for continued examination or appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider interview, appeal, RCE/continuation/divisional options; plan scope concessions carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines (prosecution timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and comply with all prosecution deadlines (responses, fees, national phase entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use docketing systems; ensure clients/inventors are aware of critical dates; missing deadlines may cause abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: When rejections cannot be overcome, consider appeal to the appropriate tribunal or board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare appellate briefs focusing on legal error and claim interpretation; weigh costs and likelihood of success versus amendment strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications, continuation applications and continuation-in-part applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Use procedural vehicles to pursue additional claims or new matter (subject to rules on added matter and priority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File divisionals to pursue separate inventions; use continuations to pursue different claim scope; CIPs may add new material but affect priority — verify jurisdictional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared for post-grant opposition or third-party challenges to granted patents in applicable forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain evidence and prosecution history to support validity; consider pre-grant strategies to minimize successful oppositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of the patent (grant formalities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand post-allowance formalities culminating in grant and issuance, including payment of grant/printing fees and possible amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with issuance requirements and renewals; confirm claim set for grant and ensure any disclaimers/amendments are properly recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent strategy: Offensive blocking patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use patenting offensively to block competitors and mount attacks on competitors' freedom-to-operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop claims targeting competitor products/processes; consider timing and scope to maximize blocking effect; prepare for enforcement costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent strategy: Defensive patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Build patents to protect freedom-to-operate, deter litigation and obtain cross-licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File strategically to cover own products and alternatives; maintain portfolios to support negotiations and defensive positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent strategy: Design-around techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate and plan for design-arounds by competitors; use claim drafting to reduce ease of design-arounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include functional and alternative claim language, parameter ranges and broad claim types to impede straightforward design-arounds; plan enforcement and licensing responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizing, educating and motivating the technical team: training management and marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Train non-technical stakeholders (management/marketing) to understand patent significance and portfolio goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide basic IP education, integrate patent strategy with business goals and involve management in disclosure/review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizing, educating and motivating the technical team: training scientists/technologists
rubrics_metrics.description: Train technical staff to identify patentable ideas, understand inventorship and prepare invention disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement inventor training, disclosure procedures and incentives; create clear channels for reporting inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting up an in-house patent review committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a committee to periodically review invention disclosures and make patenting recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define review criteria (commercial value, novelty, prosecutability), meeting cadence and decision processes; document recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor incentive programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Create programs to encourage inventors to disclose inventions and participate in patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reward structures, recognition and clear procedures for invention submission and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe ethical obligations in patent drafting, representation and client communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow jurisdictional rules for representation, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, and truthful statements to patent offices and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching prior art: patent and scientific databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct thorough prior art searches across patent databases (PATENTSCOPE, national offices) and scientific/technical literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use patent classification (IPC), keywords, applicant names and multiple-language searches; search scientific databases to capture non-patent literature that may affect novelty and inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized invention disclosure form fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect standardized information: title, field, technical problem, closest art, advantages, drawings availability, written description, inventors, testing dates, disclosure history, publications, advertisements, outside disclosures and trade shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require attachments (articles, NDAs, press releases) and complete inventorship details; use this data to evaluate patentability and prepare prosecution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing under the PCT and national phase entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the PCT to delay national filings while obtaining an international search and preliminary opinion; enter national phases according to deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand PCT publication timelines (typically 18 months), ISA competence, IPEA roles, and national phase timing and requirements; use PCT reports to refine claims before national entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding patent office documentation and databases coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarize with WIPO, national office databases and guidance (e.g., EPO Guidelines) for searching and prosecution practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PATENTSCOPE and national databases for prior art searches; consult office guidelines and PCT resources to tailor filings and responses.
